title: Conjunction: rearrange two assumptions
scope: An exact propositional equivalence; no mathematical premises are supplied implicitly.

title: Disjunction: reason by cases
scope: An exact propositional equivalence proved by considering both cases.

title: Contrapositive of an implication
scope: Proves the forward contraposition rule constructively.

title: Classical proof by contradiction
scope: Double-negation elimination uses classical reasoning; inspect the printed dependencies.

title: Negating a disjunction
scope: This De Morgan law is constructive.

title: Existence requires a witness
scope: Produces a concrete natural-number witness for a universally quantified existence statement.

title: Set intersection is commutative
scope: Sets are predicates α → Prop; the conclusion is pointwise membership equivalence.

title: Set union is associative
scope: Pointwise associativity for predicate-based sets.

title: Intersection distributes over union
scope: An exact membership equivalence; the hypotheses describe membership in three sets.

title: Subset relations compose
scope: Uses the pointwise definition of subset inclusion.

title: Preimages preserve intersections
scope: The preimage membership identity reduces to definitions.

title: Composition preserves injectivity
scope: Injectivity is stated explicitly as an equality implication.

title: Composition preserves surjectivity
scope: Surjectivity is proved by constructing preimages in reverse order.

title: A left inverse forces injectivity
scope: An elementary function theorem, not a proof that a particular matrix has an inverse.

title: A right inverse forces surjectivity
scope: A right inverse supplies the required witness directly.

title: Function composition is associative
scope: A pointwise composition identity. It does not certify a matrix algorithm.

title: Divisibility is transitive
scope: Uses a divides b as existence of a natural-number multiplier.

title: The sum of two even numbers is even
scope: Evenness is expressed by an explicit natural-number witness.

title: Adding congruences modulo a fixed number
scope: Congruence over integers is defined by the difference being an integer multiple.

title: Every natural number has parity zero or one
scope: The remainder modulo two has exactly two possibilities.

title: A finite sum splits over concatenation
scope: A recursive natural-number list sum, proved by structural induction.

title: Concatenation adds list lengths
scope: An exact statement about finite lists of arbitrary element type.

title: Mapping twice equals mapping a composition
scope: Structural induction establishes a useful finite-data transformation law.

title: A telescoping finite sum
scope: An integer-valued sequence with a recursively defined sum of consecutive differences.

title: Bounds propagate through intermediate quantities
scope: Exact integer-order transitivity; no limit passage is involved.

title: Two opposite bounds determine equality
scope: Integer antisymmetry illustrates why lower and upper bounds can pin down a value.

title: A positive integer gap excludes equality
scope: An integer gap example, not a real-analysis estimate.

title: Stepwise monotonicity controls every later term
scope: For an integer-valued sequence, adjacent inequalities imply a bound after any finite number of steps.

title: Zero consecutive differences force a constant sequence
scope: A discrete analogue only; this is not the calculus zero-derivative theorem.

title: Two eventual properties hold together eventually
scope: A quantified tail argument. It proves no convergence claim by itself.

title: Finite graph paths concatenate
scope: A graph is an arbitrary relation; reachability is its inductively defined reflexive-transitive closure.

title: Symmetric adjacency reverses a two-edge walk
scope: Only reverses a length-two walk; does not claim a general graph classification.

title: An optional value cannot be both absent and present
scope: A datatype fact underlying the abstract valuation teaching model.

title: Scaling a two-coordinate vector distributes
scope: A concrete natural-number pair model. Naturals are not a field, so this is not a general vector-space theorem.

title: The kernel of an additive map is closed under addition
scope: An exact integer additive-map statement, with additivity supplied as a hypothesis.
